- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7d horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add 3–7% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates downside; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast mean.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–3% for next 10d; if <–10%, increase by 1–3%.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact; apply 5–10% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility; use 3–5% smoothing filter on forecast slope.
